result_plain: Not enough of its spectrum was measured to compare it with asteroid types: 4 usable bands below 2.5 µm spanning 0.28 µm (at least 5 bands over 0.3 µm are needed).

geometry.note_plain: Each point is scaled to the distances and phase angle at the track's median time, from 100 orbit clones; the clones' spread is added to the errors.

hydration.verdict_plain: Not measured: SPHEREx did not see this object at 2.7-3.1 µm with enough nearby points to define the continuum.

thermal.model: Standard Thermal Model (eta 0.756, emissivity 0.9), dark surface (p_V 0.05) at the closest clone distance; points over 10% thermal are not used
thermal.note_plain: At 1.15 AU from the Sun (closest of its orbit clones) thermal emission stays below 10% at every measured wavelength, so all points are reflected sunlight.

caveats: Indicative, not definitive: a type read from a few SPHEREx colors is a hint. Confirming it needs a dedicated spectrum from a telescope.
SPHEREx starts at 0.75 µm, so it misses the visible colors that separate many subclasses. Only the broad type (S, C, X and so on) is meaningful here.
The sightings are hours apart and the asteroid rotates, so brightness changes from its shape are mixed into its colors. Every point carries an extra 8% error for this.
Spectra look redder at larger phase angles (phase reddening). That effect is not corrected.
